data.title: Somec: Strengthened €1bn Backlog, Margin Expansion, and Deleveraging Prompt Target Price Increase to €25 and Support Buy Rating
data.description:
Somec S.p.A., the Industrials sector company, was revisited by a Wall Street analyst yesterday. Analyst Alessio Olmi from TP ICAP MIDCAP maintained a Buy rating on the stock and has a €25.00 price target.

Alessio Olmi has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, starting with the sharp strengthening of Somec’s order backlog, which now exceeds €1bn after the new 350 Park Avenue glazing contract and recent wins at Fabbrica and Mestieri. This enlarged and de-risked pipeline extends revenue visibility beyond the current business plan and underpins expectations for robust H1 2026 results.

Olmi’s stance is further supported by anticipated margin expansion, driven by stricter contract selection at Mestieri, the ramp-up of Talenta, and cost efficiencies following 2025 integrations, which should lift EBITDA and net profit markedly year-on-year. Solid cash generation and a declining net debt position reinforce the balance-sheet profile, justifying the Target Price increase to €25.0 and supporting a positive view on the risk‑reward for SOM shares.

data.title: Garofalo Health Care: Buy Rating Reaffirmed as Operational Efficiency and M&A Upside Support Unchanged Target Price
data.description:
Emanuele Gallazzi, an analyst from Equita Sim, maintained the Buy rating on Garofalo Health Care S.P.A.. The associated price target is €6.20.

Emanuele Gallazzi has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors tied to both operating trends and valuation. Garofalo Health Care delivered second‑quarter results broadly in line with expectations, with revenues and adjusted EBITDA slightly ahead of forecasts and a clear improvement in profitability in the Rome operations, confirming the success of efficiency measures and the strategic reorganization underway.

At the same time, the downgrade to earnings mainly reflects more conservative, largely non‑cash provisions linked to the Gelli Law rather than a deterioration in the core business. Management has reiterated 2026 guidance, highlighted near‑term accretive M&A opportunities, and is accelerating investment in key facilities, while the shares still trade at attractive EV/EBITDA multiples relative to their defensive profile and sizable owned real‑estate portfolio, supporting upside to the unchanged target price.

data.title: Nvidia Maintained at Buy as Analyst Cites Structural AI Advantages and Reaffirms $300 Price Target
data.description:
Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider maintained a Buy rating on Nvidia yesterday and set a price target of $300.00.

James Schneider has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors tied to Nvidia’s long-term AI positioning and execution. He underscores management’s reaffirmed view that artificial intelligence could reach a total addressable market of $3 trillion to $4 trillion by 2030, driven by the industry’s shift from traditional retrieval-based computing toward generative models that demand new, specialized compute infrastructure.

Schneider also points to Nvidia’s tightly integrated hardware and networking stack as a structural advantage, particularly as Moore’s Law slows and customers seek higher performance and efficiency from AI CapEx. He highlights strong GenAI use cases in coding and cybersecurity, Nvidia’s growing share of AI investment, and its ability to manage widespread supply and datacenter capacity constraints, supporting his unchanged $300 price target and Buy recommendation.
